### 💀 Bodies fall properly now
- Everything that dies — zombies, wildlife, players — collapses into a real ragdoll instead of vanishing. Limbs fold, bodies tumble down slopes, drape over crates and slump against walls.
- The killing shot throws the body: shoot someone off a ledge and they go over it, and a headshot snaps the head back before the body drops.
- Corpses lie where they landed for a while, then quietly sink into the ground. How many stay on the map at once follows your shadow quality setting, from 3 on the lowest up to 20 on Ultra.

### 💣 Hand grenades
- Three grenades to throw, two of each, in your gear slot. Left mouse throws it properly, right mouse lobs it short and low — handy for dropping one just around a corner.
- **Fragmentation** — a 3-second fuse and a bounce, so it's for flushing out a corner or breaking up a push rather than for sniping. A direct hit hurts badly but won't outright kill a healthy player.
- **Flashbang** — no damage at all, a short fuse, and it blinds across a whole sightline. Turning away genuinely saves you: the blind depends on how close you were and whether you were looking at it.
- **Smoke** — a cloud that blooms over a second, then blocks the line of sight for about 15 seconds before thinning out. It stops eyes, not bullets, so firing blind into one is a gamble.
- Everyone sees a grenade on its way in, bouncing the same way it does for the thrower.

### 🛒 A proper buy menu for PvP
- PvP gets its own buy menu (**B**) instead of the survival inventory: pick a weapon and it goes straight into the slot it belongs in, with its spare ammo included.
- No more shopping for ammo in PvP — a gun arrives with a sensible number of spare magazines, and every respawn tops that reserve back up.
- Hovering a weapon shows its stats, which slot it would land in, and what it would replace.

### 📊 Hold Tab for full match stats
- **Tab** now opens a full stats table: kills, deaths, K/D, headshot rate, your current and best killstreak, the weapon each player is holding, zombies killed, and flag steals and returns in Capture the Flag. In Arms Race it also shows everyone's rung on the ladder.
- Your own card sits alongside it with your placement and favourite weapon, plus match highlights — most kills, longest streak, best headshot rate, most flags.
- The table marks who's dead right now and who started the room.

### ⌨️ New key layout
- **B** opens your inventory (survival) or the buy menu (PvP), and **Tab** is now the stats table you hold down.
- The mouse wheel cycles through your filled weapon slots, and there's a fifth slot.
- A "reset to defaults" button in the controls settings.
- Existing installs pick up the new layout automatically while keeping every key you bound yourself.

### ✨ Shots you can read
- Every gun throws its own tracer, so you can tell what's shooting at you from the streak alone: the bolt-action snipers fire a long cold-white needle trailing vapour, the assault rifles differ by tint, the SMG spits short pale dashes, and the shotgun's spread reads as eight stubby streaks.
- Hits on flesh spray blood in the direction the bullet was travelling and leave splatter on the ground beneath.
- A shield icon appears next to your health while your spawn protection is still up.

### 🔩 Sharper hardware
- The sentry turret is rebuilt from the ground up: three articulated legs with spiked feet, a geared turntable, a sensor pod, cooling slats, a side ammo drum, and twin barrels on their own elevation mount.
- Detail pass over the P90, pistols, assault rifles, AWP and Scout you actually stare at all match.

### ⏱️ Match start
- The pre-match countdown beeps down 3 · 2 · 1, the last beep noticeably harder than the two before, and the round opens on a shouted **Shveeskay!**
- The countdown itself is shorter — 3 seconds instead of 5.

### 🔊 Real recorded sound effects
- Every gun now fires a real recording instead of a synthesized tone — each weapon has its own report, and the snipers deliberately out-shout everything else on the map.
- Reloads are full mechanical sequences: the magazine drops out, a fresh one seats, the bolt racks. The sound follows the animation, so switching weapons mid-reload no longer leaves audio playing over a frozen hand.
- Bolt-action snipers cycle their bolt between shots — draw, lift, chamber, lock.
- Melee swings, bullet impacts, headshot hitmarkers, explosions, doors, pickups, throws and player hurt/death are all recorded takes now.
- Pulling the trigger on an empty magazine gives you a dry click.

### 👣 Footsteps that match the ground
- Footsteps and landings sound like whatever you're standing on — grass, dirt, sand, snow, stone, wood or metal. Walking across a wooden deck booms, a metal plate rings, snow just crunches.
- Climbing onto a prop or a rooftop picks up that structure's material, so you hear the surface change as you move.
- Jumping, landing and going into a crouch all have their own sound.

### 🧟 Zombies have a voice
- Zombies groan as they shamble toward you — the first warning a horde is coming is now hearing it out in the dark, well before you can see it.
- They snap their jaws when they lunge, rasp when they rake at you, grunt when your bullets land, and have a death sound of their own.
- A wave that spawns together doesn't groan in unison — each zombie keeps its own rhythm and takes, so a horde sounds like many throats.

### 🩹 The medkit is a real thing in your hands
- Healing now plays out on screen: a first-aid case opens on its hinge, a roll of gauze lifts out and unwraps over the length of the heal.
- Other players see it too — the case in your hands and the whole bandaging motion, instead of whatever weapon you had out.
